chunks: 'There is no emancipation except what is intended by it the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a divine epithet used as honorific after mentioning Allah
key_terms.عِتْق: emancipation/manumission — the act of freeing a slave, recognized as a meritorious act in Islamic law
key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: the Face of Allah — a Quranic expression meaning seeking the pleasure and approval of God

ai.seo_question: Is the emancipation of a slave valid in Islam if not intended for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that the manumission (freeing) of a slave is only legally and spiritually valid when it is performed sincerely for the sake of Allah. This ruling establishes that the intention (niyyah) is a fundamental condition for the validity of emancipation as an act of worship — a principle derived from the broader Islamic requirement that all acts of devotion and religious significance must be performed with sincerity toward God. In the early Islamic community, freeing a slave was considered one of the most meritorious acts, and this hadith clarifies that this merit is contingent on its being done purely for the divine countenance (wajh Allah), not for worldly gain or social prestige.
